arguments.summary: As of the 2026-09-22 completed session, ANET showed strong absolute momentum and positive 21- and 63-session excess returns versus both SPY and XLK. At 5 sessions, however, relative direction split: ANET outperformed SPY by 4.2931 percentage points but underperformed XLK by 0.4151 point. Price was above rising short-, medium- and long-term averages and near the prior 21-session closing high, while elevated realized volatility and a 15.5060% maximum 63-session close-path drawdown indicate substantial path risk. Historical analog positive-return frequencies in the current coarse regime were 55.4517%, 63.8629% and 65.7321% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions; each was below its corresponding unconditional base rate. These are dependent, overlapping historical observations—not calibrated forecasts.

claims.text: On 2026-09-22, ANET closed at $205.19 on the split-adjusted SIP series. Price returns were +6.4043% over 5 sessions, +8.7676% over 21 sessions and +26.5043% over 63 sessions. The close was 1.0495x SMA20, 1.0892x SMA50 and 1.3162x SMA200; RSI14 was 63.6177. This establishes absolute price strength, not benchmark leadership or intrinsic value.

PAIR ANET/SPY 5=+4.2931 21=+7.7672 63=+21.0789
PAIR ANET/XLK 5=-0.4151 21=+1.6976 63=+19.9459
Against SPY, ANET outperformed at 5, 21 and 63 sessions. Against XLK, ANET underperformed at 5 sessions but outperformed at 21 and 63 sessions. The sign reversal versus XLK means strong medium-horizon leadership coexists with a slight very-short-window sector lag.

The current regime is defined by close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50 and positive 21-session return. Conditional positive-return frequency was 55.4517% (178/321) over 5 sessions, with p10/median/p90 of -7.5762%/+0.4974%/+6.7425%, versus an unconditional 58.6207% (374/638) base rate. At 21 sessions it was 63.8629% (205/321), with -12.6204%/+2.8939%/+15.5652%, versus 68.3386% (436/638). At 63 sessions it was 65.7321% (211/321), with -20.6472%/+10.6427%/+36.7049%, versus 75.3918% (481/638). Forward windows overlap within one finite 2023-12-05 to 2026-06-23 history, making observations dependent. These are empirical analog frequencies, not calibrated forecasts, causal estimates or guarantees.

ANET's annualized realized volatility was 22.4371%, 44.8032% and 55.0458% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions. Maximum close-path drawdown over 63 sessions was -15.5060%, while the latest close was 2.5226% below the 252-session high. These are observed path-risk measures, not an earnings-risk coefficient or future-volatility forecast.

Over the latest five sessions, SMA20 rose 1.7405%. The latest close was 0.1120% below the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 0.9803x the prior 20-session median, while recent five-session average volume was 1.3679x that median. Price was pressing near a prior high with elevated recent average activity, but one latest-volume reading does not establish sustained breakout confirmation.

Continuation case: positive absolute returns at 5, 21 and 63 sessions, rising SMA20, price above SMA20/SMA50/SMA200, and positive 21- and 63-session excess returns versus both SPY and XLK support a constructive trend with medium-horizon leadership. Competing explanation: ANET may be participating in a broad technology rebound rather than starting a fresh stock-specific leg, because its 5-session excess return versus XLK was negative, it remained just below the prior 21-session closing high, and current-regime positive-return frequencies were below unconditional rates at each requested horizon. The setup therefore requires continued level and relative-strength confirmation rather than extrapolation.

gaps.description: Stronger breakout conviction requires subsequent completed-session evidence: sustained closes through the prior 21-session closing high, repeated rather than one-day volume context, and recomputed matched-window excess returns. The supplied snapshot cannot establish persistence.

assumptions: All comparisons use completed sessions through 2026-09-22, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices and price-return basis.

The historical regime is coarse; a close below SMA20, SMA20 below SMA50, or non-positive 21-session return would move ANET outside the sampled regime and invalidate direct use of these conditional analog statistics.
Forward-return observations overlap, so sample counts are not independent trials; no subjective probability or expected return is inferred.
The completed-close threshold is the frozen 2026-09-22 SMA20 level, not a future dynamic moving average and not an order instruction.
arguments.counter_thesis: The apparent medium-horizon leadership may be a volatile rebound within broad technology strength rather than durable ANET leadership. The present evidence already shows a 5-session lag versus XLK despite outperformance versus SPY. Failure to clear and hold the prior 21-session closing high, a completed close below frozen $195.506, and negative recomputed 21-session excess returns versus both SPY and XLK would strengthen the rebound-only interpretation; negative 63-session excess against both would invalidate the longer-window leadership thesis.

review_conditions.description: If ANET records a completed split-adjusted close below the frozen 2026-09-22 SMA20 level of $195.506 before expiry, treat short-term trend support as broken and downgrade the continuation interpretation to neutral/cautious pending a fresh path-panel calculation.

Recompute matched 21- and 63-session price-return excess versus both SPY and XLK. If 21-session excess turns negative against both while 63-session excess remains positive, interpret that as near-term leadership fatigue with longer-window leadership intact. If both 21- and 63-session excess turn negative against both benchmarks, invalidate the current leadership setup. Positive signs at both windows against both would confirm persistence.
